description: Students explore casting as a sculptural process across multiple material systems, including
plaster, wax, paper pulp, reusable molds, and 3D-printed molds integrated with hands-on
fabrication. The course emphasizes sustainable, low-energy materials and introduces digital
fabrication as a tool for mold-making and form development. Through studio work, readings, and
discussion, students build technical skill and conceptual grounding in contemporary casting
practices. Materials fee. Offered annually in the spring semester. Open to majors and non-majors.
